text: Decide and document whether the native kernel ABI headers and syscall surface carry a Linux-syscall-note-style exception so native userspace programs are never derivative works of the kernel.
rationale: Permissive SDK licensing and proprietary native applications rest on ambiguity unless the exception is explicit for the new ABI.

text: Institute heightened change control for Layer 1 native kernel ABI changes: mandatory RFC, compatibility review, and an ABI freeze policy per milestone.
rationale: Kernel ABI mistakes are the hardest to fix and need a stricter process than SDK changes.

text: Publish a deprecation policy per stability layer specifying notice periods and minimum supported overlap for Layer 2 interfaces.
rationale: Strong versioning is meaningless without a stated removal schedule.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Add a native kernel ABI snapshot check to CI that diffs syscall surface, object types and message layouts against a golden snapshot and fails unless the change is linked to an approved ADR.
rationale: §65 calls the ABI the most permanent decision, so accidental ABI changes must be mechanically impossible rather than caught in review.

text: Define the kernel ABI and platform interface deprecation process: announcement, minimum overlap window, tooling to detect use of deprecated interfaces.
rationale: A decades-long ABI still needs a way to retire mistakes without breaking installed software.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide the native ABI entry mechanism (syscall instruction per operation, shared submission page with rare doorbell syscalls, or vDSO-like trampolines) and set a maximum count of kernel entry points.
rationale: Entry mechanism defines syscall-overhead budgets and the size of the surface that must remain stable for decades.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Define the ABI freeze gate: golden binary compatibility test suite, fuzz corpus, documented semantics for every entry point, and a policy for adding versus changing entry points.
rationale: Without explicit freeze criteria the V1 'stable native SDK' claim has no verifiable meaning.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide whether Wayland-style ABI stability applies to Layer 2 core platform interfaces at V1 or only at 1.0, and publish the deprecation policy for each stability layer.
rationale: Developers building on V1 need to know which interfaces may still break before 1.0.

text: The native model must be capability-based, component-oriented, asynchronous and object-based; every native ABI surface is checked against these four properties.
Do not build a Linux userspace with prettier APIs; native APIs must not be thin wrappers over Linux syscalls.
Do not make the native OS POSIX-compatible; POSIX exists only inside the Linux personality.
POSIX is not the native API; no native SDK or ABI surface may be POSIX-shaped without independent justification.
Define and implement Object<T> as the fundamental typed kernel object abstraction.
Establish an ABI review gate that rejects any native interface justified only by a POSIX, Linux or Windows equivalent.
Native kernel interfaces must never exist merely because POSIX, Linux or Windows has an equivalent concept.
All three application paths (native, Linux personality, Windows personality) terminate in Native Kernel Objects; personalities ultimately sit above native primitives.
Phase B: establish two execution worlds, Native ABI and Linux ABI, selectable per component/process.
Phase B: native applications must not depend on Linux syscall semantics; verify with a syscall-filter that native components cannot invoke Linux syscalls.
The native abstraction must stay ABI-stable while its kernel implementation evolves from Linux wrappers to native code; ABI conformance tests must pass across both implementations.
The native kernel must expose typed objects Object<T> with a type identifier checked on every operation.
ADR: which Object<T> types are implemented in the kernel and which are user-service objects reached through channels, with the criteria for kernel residency.
ADR: capability handle representation in userspace (dense index, sparse id, sealed value) and its implications for hardware-assisted enforcement.
Study future memory-safe CPU architectures and record ABI assumptions that would break on them.
Do not freeze the OS around the security limitations of current x86-64 hardware; ABI review must flag any x86-64-specific assumption.
Do not make Wasm the native machine ABI.

Decide whether the Operation kind set (Read, Write, Receive, Send, Connect, Accept, Timer, Wait, GPUDispatch, DeviceOperation, StorageTransaction) is a closed kernel enum or an extensible registry that user-space services can add to, given ABI stability rules.
Decide how an Operation is identified and referenced from user space: as a Capability<Operation>, as an index in the submission ring, or as an opaque handle with a separate cancellation token.
Decide the failure encoding for Operation results (typed error enum per Operation kind vs uniform error object) so failure semantics are stable across the ABI.
The ComputeDevice ABI shape must be reserved in the native kernel ABI early enough (V1) that later hardware support does not require ABI breaks (§65).
The native platform must not assume x86-64 forever; the native ABI must be architecture-neutral in its definitions.
The native ABI must not expose page tables exactly as they exist today.
Native components must never depend on the Linux personality; the compatibility firewall (§3) must be enforced by build and lint rules.
Do not bind the OS philosophically to a single language; the native ABI and IDL must be language-neutral.
Decide the binding substrate: a stable C-compatible native ABI header plus IDL-generated per-language stubs (ADR).
Do not expose POSIX as the native ABI.
Do not expose Linux syscalls as native APIs.
Study Fuchsia/Zircon handles, rights, VMOs, channels, FIDL and component framework as the closest existing analogue of the native object model.
Study Windows NT object manager, handles, access masks and I/O request packets for object-model and Windows-personality design.
The native ABI is the project's most permanent decision; changes to it require the highest review bar in the project.
ABI rule 1: keep the kernel ABI minimal; enumerate and bound the syscall/object-operation surface.
ABI rule 2: prefer high-level semantics in userspace services rather than in the kernel ABI.
ABI rule 3: capabilities are fundamental — every object reference crossing the ABI is a Capability<T>.
ABI rule 4: async is fundamental — no blocking syscalls in the native ABI other than explicit wait-for-completion.
ABI rule 5: ownership transfer is fundamental — the ABI carries move semantics for MemoryObjects and capabilities.
ABI rule 6: versioning is fundamental — the ABI includes version identification and feature negotiation from V0.
ABI rule 7: do not expose implementation details (task_struct, mm_struct, cgroups, namespaces, page-table layout) through the native ABI.
ABI rule 8: preserve escape hatches for future hardware (capability representation, memory model, compute devices) (cross-ref §8, §38).
ABI rule 9: avoid POSIX-shaped APIs unless independently justified; each POSIX-resembling native API requires an ADR.
ABI rule 10: design the ABI to survive decades; include a formal freeze and evolution process.
ADR: native ABI shape — syscall entry mechanism, handle table design, object-operation dispatch, error model, and ABI version negotiation.
Native ABI specification document, normative, versioned, with every syscall/object-op defined.
Because kernel ABI mistakes are harder to fix than SDK mistakes, any Layer 1 change must ship with a deprecation strategy and compatibility shim plan.
Define Layer 1 (native kernel ABI) scope: extremely small and extremely stable; enumerate which primitives are in it.
Decide which concepts are Layer 1 versus Layer 2 (e.g. is the compositor protocol Layer 2? is the package format Layer 2? are ResourceDomain policies Layer 1?).
Principle 14: native architecture must accommodate future hardware without redesigning the world.
Linux-derived kernel: Native ABI entry layer.

Defining constraint: do not fossilize at 2026 — the 1.0 gate must include a fossilization review of the ABI, MemoryObject, ComputeDevice and capability representation against future-hardware scenarios (CXL, CHERI, NPUs, disaggregated memory).
